title: System Voltage Malfunction (Extended)
shortDescription: PCM sees a system battery voltage value outside the valid operating window.
fullDescription: PCM sees a system battery voltage value outside the valid operating window. Sensor reference, system voltage, and power-relay codes are almost always wiring-driven. A single shorted or water-damaged sensor can pull a 5V reference low and trip multiple unrelated codes; a marginal main relay or corroded ground stud can drive the entire power-supply family. Always inspect harness routing and grounds first.
safetyImpact: Voltage and reference faults can cascade into stalling, no-start, or unexpected limp mode while driving.

causes.cause: Shorted sensor pulling reference voltage low

fixSteps.title: Test battery and charging
fixSteps.instruction: Battery should rest at 12.6V and charge between 13.8 and 14.7V. Replace battery or alternator before chasing reference codes.

fixSteps.title: Voltage-drop the grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Run a voltage-drop test from battery negative to engine block, body, and PCM ground stud under load. Anything > 0.1V is suspect.

fixSteps.title: Isolate the reference
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug sensors one at a time on the affected reference circuit. If reference voltage recovers when one sensor is unplugged, that sensor is shorted internally.

fixSteps.title: Inspect main relay & wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the main relay with a known-good identical unit. Inspect the engine harness for chafe points, especially where the harness rounds the cylinder head or transmission bell housing.

faq.q: Should I just replace the PCM?
faq.a: No — PCM internal faults are the rarest cause. Verify power, ground, and reference circuits first.

faq.q: Why do I have so many other codes?
faq.a: When a reference circuit is pulled out of range, every sensor that shares it sets its own code. Fix the reference and the rest will clear.

A single shorted or water-damaged sensor can pull a 5V reference low and trip multiple unrelated codes; a marginal main relay or corroded ground stud can drive the entire power-supply family. Always inspect harness routing and grounds first.
safetyImpact: Voltage and reference faults can cascade into stalling, no-start, or unexpected limp mode while driving.

causes.cause: Shorted sensor pulling reference voltage low

fixSteps.title: Test battery and charging
fixSteps.instruction: Battery should rest at 12.6V and charge between 13.8 and 14.7V. Replace battery or alternator before chasing reference codes.

fixSteps.title: Voltage-drop the grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Run a voltage-drop test from battery negative to engine block, body, and PCM ground stud under load. Anything > 0.1V is suspect.

fixSteps.title: Isolate the reference
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug sensors one at a time on the affected reference circuit. If reference voltage recovers when one sensor is unplugged, that sensor is shorted internally.

fixSteps.title: Inspect main relay & wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the main relay with a known-good identical unit. Inspect the engine harness for chafe points, especially where the harness rounds the cylinder head or transmission bell housing.

faq.q: Should I just replace the PCM?
faq.a: No — PCM internal faults are the rarest cause. Verify power, ground, and reference circuits first.

faq.q: Why do I have so many other codes?
faq.a: When a reference circuit is pulled out of range, every sensor that shares it sets its own code. Fix the reference and the rest will clear.
